facts.text: On this date in 1380, Dmitry Donskoy's forces defeated the Mongol Golden Horde at Kulikovo — the first major Russian military victory over the Mongols, after 140 years of subjugation.
On Sept 8, 1943, Italy's armistice with the Allies was announced publicly. Within hours, the German army began occupying Rome, turning a surrender into an invasion.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Manila with a 1,500 km radius than exist in the entire Western Hemisphere.
Lesotho is the only country on Earth where every single point of land sits above 1,000 meters — it has no lowlands whatsoever.
Tokyo's greater metro area produces an economy larger than the entire GDP of Canada, generated by a region covering less than 1% of Japan's land.
On this date in 1998, Google was incorporated in a Menlo Park garage with $100,000 in seed money. It went public six years later at $85 a share.
On Sept 8, 1873, the Vienna Stock Exchange crashed, triggering a global depression that lasted longer than the Great Depression of the 1930s.
The entire U.S. Treasury bond market — roughly $27 trillion — turns over in about 60 days. It is the most liquid market on Earth, and it still hiccuped in March 2020.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway once traded below $8 a share. A single Class A share now costs more than most Americans earn in a decade.
The Dutch East India Company paid dividends continuously for nearly 200 years, surviving wars, famines, and piracy — then collapsed almost overnight in 1799.
On this date in 1966, Star Trek premiered — and its communicator inspired the flip phone. The show's writers invented the badge-tap interface too, which Motorola later patented almost verbatim.
Your femur is stronger than concrete. A cubic inch of bone can withstand roughly 19,000 pounds of compressive force before fracturing.

On September 8, 2004, NASA's Genesis capsule crashed into the Utah desert when its parachute failed — yet scientists still recovered enough solar wind particles to rewrite models of the Sun's composition.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh approximately one billion tons on Earth.
Octopuses have three hearts, blue blood, and neurons distributed throughout their arms — each limb can taste, touch, and make decisions independently of the brain.
On this day in 1504, Michelangelo's David was unveiled in Florence — older than the Ottoman conquest of Egypt, older than the Americas having a name, older than the guitar in any recognizable form.
On this day in 1966, Star Trek premiered. It debuted closer in time to the end of World War II than to today.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, making it older than the telephone, the light bulb, and every country in the Americas except the United States.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid she would have visited as a tourist.
The University of Oxford began teaching in 1096 — it was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012 — and already feels indispensable.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Also Koenig's coinage — proof that naming a feeling summons the courage to admit you've always had it.
On this day in 1941, the Siege of Leningrad began. The Russian word 'blokada' — blockade — entered the city's collective memory so deeply it still means that siege, and only that siege.
Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or never had. Untranslatable because English presumes every home is recoverable.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word from Tierra del Fuego meaning the look shared by two people who both want something but neither will initiate. The language has one living native speaker.
On this date in 2017, China's central bank declared ICOs illegal, triggering a 40% crash in ETH within days — then the market fully recovered within six weeks.
On this date in 2021, El Salvador made Bitcoin legal tender, the first nation to do so — but its IMF loan deal three years later quietly required scaling back BTC's mandatory acceptance.
Bitcoin's smallest unit, the satoshi, wasn't named by Satoshi Nakamoto — the community coined the term in a 2010 BitcoinTalk thread, months after Nakamoto had already gone silent.
The Ethereum genesis block contains a hidden message: the hash of a New York Times headline about bank bailouts, a direct echo of Bitcoin's own embedded block-zero timestamp.
Vitalik Buterin published the Ethereum whitepaper at 19. By the time the mainnet launched in 2015, he was 21 — younger than most startup founders when they incorporate.
On this date in 2016, DeepMind's WaveNet paper was published — a generative audio model so compute-hungry that it initially produced one second of speech per ten minutes of processing time.

On this date in 2022, the U.S. National Security Commission on AI had already warned Congress that China would surpass American AI capabilities by 2025 unless export controls on advanced chips were enacted.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of about 4,600 average U.S. households.

The 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Hopfield and Hinton for foundational work on neural networks — the first time the physics prize recognized research with no direct connection to physical phenomena.

Transformers, now the dominant architecture in AI, were originally proposed in 2017 solely for machine translation; the authors did not anticipate their application to images, protein folding, or code generation.
